blocks.html: A. Request for Reconsideration

blocks.text: The AMCD will provide initial reconsideration. Some cases may be referred to the appropriate RFS for action. If the AMCD or a RFS finds that the applicant is not qualified, the applicant is denied and advised of further reconsideration and appeal procedures. These may include reconsideration by the Federal Air Surgeon and/or petition for NTSB review.

blocks.text: B. Statement of Demonstrated Ability (SODA)
blocks.html: B. Statement of Demonstrated Ability (SODA)

blocks.text: At the discretion of the Federal Air Surgeon, a Statement of Demonstrated Ability (SODA) may be granted, instead of an Authorization, to a person whose disqualifying condition is static or non-progressive and who has been found capable of performing airman duties without endangering public safety. A SODA does not expire and authorizes a designated AME to issue a medical certificate of a specified class if the AME finds that the condition described on the SODA has not adversely changed.
blocks.html: At the discretion of the Federal Air Surgeon, a Statement of Demonstrated Ability (SODA) may be granted, instead of an Authorization, to a person whose disqualifying condition is static or non-progressive and who has been found capable of performing airman duties without endangering public safety. A SODA does not expire and authorizes a designated AME to issue a medical certificate of a specified class if the AME finds that the condition described on the SODA has not adversely changed.

blocks.text: In granting a SODA , the Federal Air Surgeon may consider the person's operational experience and any medical facts that may affect the ability of the person to perform airman duties including:
blocks.html: In granting a SODA , the Federal Air Surgeon may consider the person's operational experience and any medical facts that may affect the ability of the person to perform airman duties including:

blocks.text: - The combined effect on the person of failure to meet more than one requirement of part 67; and
blocks.html: • The combined effect on the person of failure to meet more than one requirement of part 67; and

blocks.text: - The prognosis derived from professional consideration of all available information regarding the person.
blocks.html: • The prognosis derived from professional consideration of all available information regarding the person.

blocks.text: In granting a SODA under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401), the Federal Air Surgeon specifies the class of medical certificate authorized to be issued and may do any of the following:
blocks.html: In granting a SODA under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401), the Federal Air Surgeon specifies the class of medical certificate authorized to be issued and may do any of the following:

blocks.text: - State on the SODA , and on any medical certificate based upon it, any operational limitation needed for safety; or
blocks.html: • State on the SODA , and on any medical certificate based upon it, any operational limitation needed for safety; or

blocks.text: - Condition the continued effect of a SODA, and any second- or third-class medical certificate based upon it, on compliance with a statement of functional limitations issued to the person in coordination with the Director of Flight Standards or the Director's designee.
blocks.html: • Condition the continued effect of a SODA, and any second- or third-class medical certificate based upon it, on compliance with a statement of functional limitations issued to the person in coordination with the Director of Flight Standards or the Director's designee.

blocks.text: - In determining whether a SODA should be granted to an applicant for a third-class medical certificate, the Federal Air Surgeon considers the freedom of an airman, exercising the privileges of a private pilot certificate, to accept reasonable risks to his or her person and property that are not acceptable in the exercise of commercial or airline transport pilot privileges, and, at the same time, considers the need to protect the safety of persons and property in other aircraft and on the ground.
blocks.html: • In determining whether a SODA should be granted to an applicant for a third-class medical certificate, the Federal Air Surgeon considers the freedom of an airman, exercising the privileges of a private pilot certificate, to accept reasonable risks to his or her person and property that are not acceptable in the exercise of commercial or airline transport pilot privileges, and, at the same time, considers the need to protect the safety of persons and property in other aircraft and on the ground.

blocks.text: A SODA granted to a person who does not meet the applicable standards of part 67 may be withdrawn, at the discretion of the Federal Air Surgeon, at any time if:
blocks.html: A SODA granted to a person who does not meet the applicable standards of part 67 may be withdrawn, at the discretion of the Federal Air Surgeon, at any time if:

blocks.text: - There is adverse change in the holder's medical condition;
blocks.html: • There is adverse change in the holder's medical condition;

blocks.text: - The holder fails to comply with a statement of functional limitations or operational limitations issued under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401);
blocks.html: • The holder fails to comply with a statement of functional limitations or operational limitations issued under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401);

blocks.text: - Public safety would be endangered by the holder's exercise of airman privileges;
blocks.html: • Public safety would be endangered by the holder's exercise of airman privileges;

blocks.text: - The holder fails to provide medical information reasonably needed by the Federal Air Surgeon for certification under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401);
blocks.html: • The holder fails to provide medical information reasonably needed by the Federal Air Surgeon for certification under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401);

blocks.text: - The holder makes or causes to be made a statement or entry that is the basis for withdrawal of a SODA under the falsification section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.403); or
blocks.html: • The holder makes or causes to be made a statement or entry that is the basis for withdrawal of a SODA under the falsification section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.403); or

blocks.text: - A person who has been granted a SODA under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401), based on a special medical flight or practical test need not take the test again during later medical examinations unless the Federal Air Surgeon determines or has reason to believe that the physical deficiency has or
blocks.html: • A person who has been granted a SODA under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401), based on a special medical flight or practical test need not take the test again during later medical examinations unless the Federal Air Surgeon determines or has reason to believe that the physical deficiency has or

blocks.text: may have degraded to a degree to require another special medical flight test or practical test.
blocks.html: may have degraded to a degree to require another special medical flight test or practical test.

blocks.text: The authority of the Federal Air Surgeon under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401) is also exercised by the Manager, AMCD, and each RFS.
blocks.html: The authority of the Federal Air Surgeon under the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401) is also exercised by the Manager, AMCD, and each RFS.

blocks.text: If a SODA is withdrawn at any time, the following procedures apply:
blocks.html: If a SODA is withdrawn at any time, the following procedures apply:

blocks.text: - The holder of the SODA will be served a letter of withdrawal stating the reason for the action;
blocks.html: • The holder of the SODA will be served a letter of withdrawal stating the reason for the action;

blocks.text: - By not later than 60 days after the service of the letter of withdrawal, the holder of the SODA may request, in writing, that the Federal Air Surgeon provide for review of the decision to withdraw. The request for review may be accompanied by supporting medical evidence;
blocks.html: • By not later than 60 days after the service of the letter of withdrawal, the holder of the SODA may request, in writing, that the Federal Air Surgeon provide for review of the decision to withdraw. The request for review may be accompanied by supporting medical evidence;

blocks.text: - Within 60 days of receipt of a request for review, a written final decision either affirming or reversing the decision to withdraw will be issued; and
blocks.html: • Within 60 days of receipt of a request for review, a written final decision either affirming or reversing the decision to withdraw will be issued; and

blocks.text: - A medical certificate rendered invalid pursuant to a withdrawal, in accordance with the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401 (a)) shall be surrendered to the Administrator upon request.
blocks.html: • A medical certificate rendered invalid pursuant to a withdrawal, in accordance with the special issuance section of part 67 (14 CFR 67.401 (a)) shall be surrendered to the Administrator upon request.

blocks.text: C. National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB)
blocks.html: C. National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB)

blocks.text: Within 60 days after a final FAA denial of an unrestricted airman medical certificate, an airman may petition the NTSB for a review of that denial. The NTSB does not have jurisdiction to review the denial of a SODA or special issuance airman medical certificate.
blocks.html: Within 60 days after a final FAA denial of an unrestricted airman medical certificate, an airman may petition the NTSB for a review of that denial. The NTSB does not have jurisdiction to review the denial of a SODA or special issuance airman medical certificate.

blocks.text: A petition for NTSB review must be submitted in writing to:
blocks.html: A petition for NTSB review must be submitted in writing to:

blocks.text: National Transportation Safety Board
blocks.html: National Transportation Safety Board

blocks.text: 490 L'Enfant Plaza, East SW
blocks.html: 490 L'Enfant Plaza, East SW

blocks.text: Washington, DC 20594-0001
blocks.html: Washington, DC 20594-0001

blocks.text: The NTSB is an independent agency of the Federal Government that has the authority to review on appeal the suspension, amendment, modification, revocation, or denial of any certificate or license issued by the FAA Administrator.
blocks.html: The NTSB is an independent agency of the Federal Government that has the authority to review on appeal the suspension, amendment, modification, revocation, or denial of any certificate or license issued by the FAA Administrator.

blocks.text: An Administrative Law Judge for the NTSB may hold a formal hearing at which the FAA will present documentary evidence and testimony by medical specialists supporting the denial decision. The petitioner will also be given an opportunity to present evidence and testimony at the hearing. The Administrative Law Judge’s decision is subject to review by the full NTSB.
